scope: Bounded read-only depth research for Bhukha, Sadhu Meher and Manmohan Mahapatra; no film viewing

findings.access: Original catalogue synopsis recovered in search index; direct PDF timeout
facts: Ankur's Kishtaya is a poor potter, husband of Laxmi; landlord's son Surya becomes involved with her after Kishtaya leaves following public punishment.
Kishtaya returns with earnings and accepts her approaching motherhood. He approaches Surya for work and is whipped; Laxmi intervenes.
findings.use: Add a concise account of economic vulnerability and the final conflict, attributed to the catalogue. Use modern respectful terminology rather than reproducing dated disability language.
findings.budget: Existing article derives approximately 67 words from this source. Keep additions plus note under the 200-word aggregate.

findings.access: Page opened; indexed synopsis also captured

Describes class oppression and physical assault as central to the story.
findings.limits: Use cast-role mapping and synopsis only; page runtime/category fields are inconsistent. No streaming or complete-viewing claim.

findings.authority: 1985 Indian Panorama catalogue, Klanta Aparanha entry
findings.access: Full synopsis recovered in indexed primary-source extract; direct PDF unavailable
facts: Retired Adikanda lives in a village with his mother and daughter Niru.
Niru teaches with Sandhya and Veena, who share rented accommodation; the women exchange news and hopes.
Adikanda mortgages land to arrange money for the anticipated marriage proposal and dowry.
findings.use: Concrete story details show economic pressure and women's lives more clearly than a generic rural-cinema description.
findings.budget: Existing derived aggregate approximately 100 words; a 60–70-word synopsis remains feasible if redundant methodological prose is removed.
findings.limits: The 1984 and 1985 catalogue biographies give differing Seeta Raati dates. Keep any 1976 claim explicitly attributed; do not infer release chronology.

findings.authority: Himanshu Guru interview/report, OrissaPOST, 31 October 2016, 'Reel lights' section
findings.access: Page opened and director quotation recovered
facts: Sabyasachi Mohapatra identifies Sadhu Meher as Bhukha's protagonist.
He explains using a lantern inside the protagonist's home to express the limited means of a family of folk artistes.
findings.use: Attribute the visual choice to the director's account; do not imply independent viewing of the scene.
findings.limits: Do not generalize the lighting choice to all rural households or use unrelated dates in the article.

findings.authority: OdishaPlus interview with Sabyasachi Mohapatra, 15 July 2022
findings.access: Full page opened; relevant exchange near lines 259–261
facts: Director recalls Bhukha doing well in western Odisha and in Bhubaneswar, Cuttack and Puri.
Discusses the separate costs of promotion and distribution when explaining later release decisions.
findings.limits: Reception is the director's recollection, not independently audited box office. Do not transfer his later-career distribution difficulties to Bhukha as an established production fact. Avoid unrelated erroneous award wording in the interview caption.
